kjv: I (Yahweh) remember that which Amalek did
mine: I (Yahweh) have taken note of what Amalek did
note: Hebrew paqadti means "I have attended to / I am calling to account", the language of reckoning and punishment, which is stronger than mere remembering.
Hebrew vayyichar le-Shemu'el is the idiom for burning anger (charah), though it may be anger mixed with distress; "grieved" softens it.
Hebrew nichamti, "I regret / I am sorry"; to a modern reader "repent" implies turning from sin, which the text does not ascribe to God (the same verb recurs in vv. 29 and 35).

kjv: he (Saul) set him up a place
mine: he (Saul) set up a monument for himself
note: Hebrew yad ("hand") here means a memorial stela, as in 2 Sam 18:18 (Absalom's monument); "a place" obscures Saul's self-glorification.
Hebrew qesem is divination (seeking omens, cf. 1 Sam 6:2; 28:8), not witchcraft in the sense of casting spells.
Hebrew netsach yisra'el is a unique title; netsach means "eminence, glory, perpetuity" and is rendered variously as Glory, Eternal One, or Strength.

Hebrew ma'adannot is obscure: from 'adan "delight" it suggests cheerfully or confidently (matching his words), while others read it as "in fetters" (cf. Job 38:31); "delicately" now suggests fragility.
